title: Comfrey salve for sprains
subtitle: An external-use salve for sprains, bruising, and muscle strain
excerpt: Dried comfrey leaf infused into olive oil, then set with beeswax at a 1:4 ratio. For external use on sprains, bruising, and muscle strain only. Never ingested. Do not apply to broken skin. Use for up to 10 days continuously on the same area.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), Comfrey (Symphytum officinale) entry : external vulnerary use and allantoin content. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Symphytum officinale (2011, updated 2015) .  external-use-only guidance and 10-day course limit based on pyrrolizidine alkaloid content. Note: older sources including Maud Grieve describe internal use of comfrey; this preparation is external-only in accordance with the modern EMA guidance on pyrrolizidine alkaloid safety.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Salve keeps for 12 months in a sealed tin in a cool dark place. Prepare in a single session using the double-boiler oil method.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Store in a sealed tin in a cool dark place. Discard if the surface develops white spots or the salve smells rancid.

glossaryTerms.definition: A compound found in comfrey leaf associated in traditional western herbal practice with supporting tissue healing when applied externally.
Compounds present in comfrey root and leaf that are harmful to the liver when ingested. They are not significantly absorbed through intact skin at the concentrations used in a properly made salve.

content.text: Comfrey salve is a firm external preparation made from dried Symphytum officinale leaf infused into olive oil, then combined with beeswax to set. Applied to the skin over a sprain, bruise, or strained muscle, it is in tradition linked to help tissue healing through its allantoin content. This is an external-use preparation only: comfrey contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids that are hepatotoxic (damaging to the liver) if ingested. The salve must never be swallowed or used on the face of infants. External use on intact skin, at this preparation level, is accepted in modern western herbal practice.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body:
Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor for ongoing or serious symptoms.

EXTERNAL USE ONLY. Comfrey contains pyrrolizidine alkaloids that are damaging to the liver when ingested. Never eat, drink, or swallow any preparation of comfrey. Keep out of reach of children and away from food preparation surfaces.

Do not apply this salve to broken, open, or infected skin. Comfrey promotes tissue repair quickly; applied over an open wound it can seal the surface before the tissue beneath has healed, which can trap infection.

Do not apply to open wounds or burns of any kind.

Do not apply to the face of infants.

Do not use on the same area of skin continuously for more than 10 days.

If you are in doubt about the severity of a sprain, bruise, or muscle injury, seek medical assessment before applying any home remedy.

Paediatric use is not adult-divided-by-half. Consult a herbalist who specialises in children's herbal medicine before using on children under twelve.

content.text: Place 20 g of dried comfrey leaf and 100 ml of olive oil into the top vessel of a double boiler. Stir to combine.
Heat over a low flame. Use a probe thermometer to hold the oil at 60-65°C. Maintain this temperature for 2-4 hours. The oil should turn green-brown and smell of the herb.
Remove from the heat. Cool for 10 minutes, then strain through muslin cloth into a measuring jug, pressing the cloth to extract all the oil.
Return the strained oil to the clean double boiler. Add 25 g of beeswax pellets and warm gently, stirring, until fully melted.
Check the set by dropping a small amount onto a cold saucer. Adjust with more beeswax if too soft, or a little more oil if too hard.
Pour into clean salve tins. Leave undisturbed for 30 minutes to set. Label clearly with the contents and the date, and the words EXTERNAL USE ONLY.

Apply a thin layer to the intact skin over the affected area up to three times a day. Do not use on the same area of skin continuously for more than 10 days. For a new sprain or bruise, start from the first day of injury. For muscle strain, apply after exercise or as soreness arises.

Store in a sealed tin in a cool dark place, clearly labelled EXTERNAL USE ONLY. The salve keeps for 12 months. Discard if the surface develops white spots or the smell turns rancid. Keep out of reach of children and away from food preparation areas.
When not to use this remedy
Do not use on open wounds, broken skin, infected areas, or burns. Do not use on the face of infants. Do not ingest under any circumstances.

See a doctor for sudden severe muscle pain, muscle pain with dark urine, muscle pain with weakness, or pain that is disproportionate to any injury. See A&E for a suspected fracture, severe sprain with inability to bear weight, or any injury where something may be broken.
See a doctor for unexplained bruising, frequent bruising, bruising with bleeding gums or nosebleeds, or bruising in unusual sites. Clotting disorders need assessment.
